newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Monti hopes for progress on tax issues in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Monti hopes for progress on tax issues in 1997.

text.p: European Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti said on Wednesday he was hopeful that the EU would be able to achieve a higher degree of tax coordination by the end of the year.

He said a group of high-level national tax experts created recently to tackle harmful tax competition within the European Union would meet for the second time on May 6 with the view of drafting a code of conduct.

Work in the group would be based on data provided by all EU states on examples of unfair tax competition, the sectors harmed and the size of the problem, Monti told a news conference to present a plan to complete the single market by 1999.

He said the Dutch EU presidency had shown a great interest in making progress on the issue and that Luxembourg, which will replace the Netherlands in the second half of 1997, was committed to show that it was not holding up agreement on tax proposals.
Monti said there was a need for more tax cooperation, especially concerning the taxation of capital income, an issue which has angered Germany and Belgium against tax-haven Luxembourg.
"A well-functioning single market does require a degree of harmonisation in the field of taxation of capital income," he said adding that he favoured a "minimum withholding rate".
The EU dropped in 1994 a draft directive for a withholding tax on income from capital such as interests on savings in the face of strong opposition from Luxembourg but also Britain.
Monti said Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker was now open to a discussion that would embrace also the statute of off-shore centres.
"Juncker has a sympathy for this package approach," he told reporters after the conference.
A code of conduct would not prevent the Commission from initiating new laws.
"I see a code of conduct not inconsistent with legislative measures. There will be legislative measures," Monti said,
"I expect important progress in the course of this year".
The high level tax group will meet again on June 6. It first met in March.
